evaluator: Fictionalized Margaret Morse analytical lens only. I am not Margaret Morse, do not speak for Margaret Morse, and this is not an endorsement.
evidence: The homepage and About page establish a rushed-reader threshold: Jamie is immediately identified as a technical project manager, while the explicit through line describes an artistic, civic, technical, and social practice concerned with systems people can inhabit.

196 Artists Residency / Sunday Dinner accurately delimits participation, hospitality, care, embodiment, and continuity through 300+ gatherings, 20+ resident artists, hosting, food, space, welcome, onboarding, facilitation, minimal documentation, and protected participant records.

NYC Artist Coalition / FairRentNYC connects civic participation, technical implementation, attention, documentation, and place through campaign websites, source maps, meeting memory, working sessions at Shoestring Press, and a collective town hall at Market Hotel.

WOWList.org supplies a third delimited example of technical and social experimentation: a collaboratively editable natural-language calendar organized around community vocabulary, used by local organizers across 35 city ecosystems, with Richard Caceres explicitly credited as co-founder and co-builder.

Open House is expressly bounded as a ten-day UCSC gallery experiment in communal living and participatory art, making the artistic lineage visible without converting it into an unsupported current deployment claim.

The Technical Operations page and exact public resume make the target role legible through requirements, delivery coordination, UAT/QA, risk and dependency tracking, implementation, launch, adoption, operating documentation, and durable handoffs.

Collective authorship remains intact through repeated collaborator and community credits, explicit statements that campaign outcomes were collective, and careful separation of Jamie's implementation responsibilities from movement accomplishments.

Participant privacy remains intact: Sunday Dinner publishes workflow reconstructions without participant-level values, WOW List withholds private user and organizer data, and FairRentNYC omits private strategy, legal-review, stakeholder, and correspondence material.
Rendered-image descriptions provide dates, places, photographers or courtesy credits, and collective context; nothing in the packet implies participant endorsement or compromises dignity.
safety_findings: No protected praise, private-record content, participant identity, or named-professor endorsement is inferred.

Photograph captions preserve attribution, contextual integrity, and collective-work boundaries; the supplied release-audit context confirms candidate-specific portfolio clearance while leaving production release and indexing as separate gates.
Historical, archived, current, proposed, and protected material is consistently distinguished, limiting misleading claims of present deployment or adoption.
recommendation: Pass the PR-015 public-surface holdout. No public-surface change is required to clear this lens; production release and indexing remain separate decisions.
